newsitem.title: UK: British retail sales grow strongly in April - survey.
newsitem.headline: British retail sales grow strongly in April - survey.

text.p: British retail sales grew strongly in April but competition between shops remained strong and price pressures were subdued, the British Retail Consortium said on Monday.
Its monthly sales monitor said the value of sales rose by 4.1 percent in the year to April on a like-for-like basis, up from 3.7 percent in March.
But the average rate of increase in the three months to April slowed to 4.0 percent, the lowest underlying rate of increase recorded since late 1995.
"Low value growth reflects the very subdued rate of inflation in the retail sector with retail goods inflation of just 0.9 percent recorded in March accompanying steady volume growth," it said.
The report said mixed weather was the dominant factor for many retailers whose sales were "good while the sun shone".
Computers and games consoles continued to sell strongly while furniture orders reflected healthy consumer demand.
Andrew Higginson, chairman of the BRC economic affairs committee, said while trading conditions were positive, price competition was keen.
"Consumers are benefitting particularly from lower food prices. Post election the main uncertainties are the impact of higher interest rates and the prospect of a budget in the early summer."
Andrew Sentance, chief economic advier to the BRC, said future spending may be restained by the prospect of the budget and interest rates .
"Last week's rise in interest rates and speculation about tax rises in the budget are both likely to hold back spending in May and June."

He said how the consumer recovery develops in the second half of the year will hinge on future interest rate decisions, the shape of the new Chancellor's first budget and consumers willingness to spend windfall gains from building society conversions.
